application_guidance.input_pattern: An already certified true-distance-sensitive strong solver on the same original domain and oracle model.
read_original_when: Changing the orbit, prediction, stepsize schedule or inner error sequence
Replacing firm nonexpansiveness, exact jets, norms or domain operations
Seeking independent reproof of the block energy estimates
sensitive_conditions: Fixed eta and one fixed analytical resolvent throughout the orbit
Both exponent inequalities, including the a=2/3 endpoint
Genuine normal and saved final evaluated value
Interrupt before the next original query in every descendant
Aggregate energy cannot be replaced by an unsupported pointwise claim

complexity_scope.guarantee: Guaranteed success under a valid distance promise; finite capped behavior and sound successful acceptance under a false distance promise.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Known recursively chosen constants for the fixed interface; no dimension dependence, uniform-in-p assertion, arithmetic or bit-complexity bound.
complexity_scope.oracle: Complete feasible exact order-p jets; a known affine regularization costs one original-F query per nested jet.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Evaluated (yhatK,nK,F(yhatK)) with yhatK in X, nK in N_X(yhatK), ||F(yhatK)+nK||<=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: Fixed exponents with 0<gamma<=1 and 2/3<=(p-1)gamma<=2; positive accuracy and 0<R<=D.
complexity_scope.resource: Worst-case total original-query count, including K+1 inner solves, startup, radius discovery, all descendants and final certificate evaluation; no extra query for saved-value affine subtraction.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Algorithm 5 consuming the established S_gamma,b interface; an upper-interface transformation, not a lower bound.

content.intended_use: One acyclic boost in the finite higher-order VI hierarchy.

map: Section 7 p.19 constructs the analytical P_eta=(I+eta(F+N_X))^-1, establishes existence/uniqueness and firm nonexpansiveness from the VI inclusions. It is used for analysis, not as a free queried operation.

Lemma 6.1 p.18 bounds first differences and the exact Halpern residual for one fixed map. Lemma 6.2 p.19 applies firm nonexpansiveness to successive inputs, telescopes the squared first differences and bounds cross terms. It obtains block second-difference energy <=64 R^2(1+H_{2k})^2/k^2. Remark 6.3 explicitly excludes a pointwise accelerated interpretation.

Section 7.1 p.21 uses strong monotonicity of each Gt and the inner certificate to obtain ||yhatt-P_eta(xt)||<=eta delta=e. Nonexpansiveness and the Halpern update give ||xt-xbart||<=te/2 and ||yhatt-ybart||<=(t+2)e/2.

Lemma 7.1 projects the linear prediction onto X and compares it to the exact shadow orbit: r_t<=||ybart-2 ybar_{t-1}+ybar_{t-2}||+(2t+1)e. The startup bound r0,r1<=3R and Lemma 6.2 yield block sum r_t^2<=256 R^2(1+H_{2k})^2/k^2. The perturbation contribution is at most 50 k^3 e^2 and is absorbed using e=R/(K+2)^4.

Lemma 7.2 p.21 retains the final genuine nK and writes F(yhatK)+nK=vK-(yhatK-xK)/eta. Equation (7.10) bounds its norm by eta^-1[2R(1+H_{K+1})/(K+1)+(K+2)e], which is below epsilon with the specified eta,e. This includes the final inner solve.

Theorem 8.1 p.22 first considers the uncapped run. For 0<a<=2, power mean on each dyadic block gives sum r_t^a<=k^(1-a/2)(sum r_t^2)^(a/2)<=16^a R^a(1+H_{2k})^a k^(1-3a/2). Include t=0,1 with 2*3^a and sum the actual possibly truncated blocks to obtain sum_{t=0}^K r_t^a<=R^a U_a(K). Summing the S interface costs gives equation (8.7), below B. Thus the installed cap cannot interrupt a valid run.

Because 1-3a/2<=0, dyadic summation yields equation (8.6): sum r_t^a<=C_p R^a[1+log(K+2)]^(a+1), including the equality endpoint. This is aggregate accounting and includes all startup solves and distance-radius discovery.

On p.23 set h=1+H_{K+1}. The three dimensionless log terms are eta Lp D^(p-1)=8h Q_R(D/R)^(p-1)/(K+1), Lp D^p/(e/eta)=8h Q_R(K+2)^4(D/R)^p/(K+1), and ((1/eta)D)/(e/eta)=(D/R)(K+2)^4. Hence L_S<=C_p L_A and 1+log(K+2)<=C_p L_A. Since eta Lp R^(p-1)=8h Q_R/(K+1), a+1+gamma<=4 yields (8.9). Balance gamma(1-alpha)=alpha to obtain the stated rate.

The same block majorant bounds the explicit public cap even without a valid promise. Shared descendant counting ensures finite interruption; the final evaluated norm test ensures sound acceptance. This is precisely the capped residual contract required by the published restart theorem.
proofs.omitted_details: This is a precise source-linked map of the literature argument, not a full independent reproof of all orbit estimates or a Lean check. The lower-level S implementation is an explicit input contract, not a future hierarchy assumption.
proofs.reading_coverage: Current-role direct original PDF text pp.7–10,16–23 and actual attached images pp.19–23; no whole-paper reading claimed.

assumptions: Fixed integer p>=2, fixed b>=0 and fixed 0<gamma<=1 with a=(p-1)gamma in [2/3,2]. The S_gamma,b interface is already constructed for the same domain, regularity and original-query model, with a known instance-independent leading constant C_S.
Lp,D,epsilon>0, 0<R<=D. For guaranteed success some VI solution satisfies ||x0-zstar||<=R.

Exact feasible queries return complete jets through D^(p-1). Known-domain projections and exact computations on returned Taylor data are internal operations. Every original query, including nested and certificate queries, is charged.

Inner outputs have genuine original-domain normals and saved evaluated values; no claim is inferred from distance alone. All active caps propagate to descendants and interrupt before the next prohibited original query.
Use Algorithm 5 with one eta fixed for the entire run, K+1 inner calls and the explicit public cap below.
statement.conclusion: Set alpha=gamma/(1+gamma), K=max{2,ceil(Q_R^alpha)}, e=R/(K+2)^4, eta=8R(1+H_{K+1})/[epsilon(K+1)], delta=e/eta. Define U_a(K)=2*3^a+16^a sum_{j=1}^{floor(log_2 K)}(1+H_{2^{j+1}})^a 2^{j(1-3a/2)} and B=ceil(C_S L_S(1/eta,e/eta)^b[K+1+(eta Lp)^gamma R^a U_a(K)])+1. Algorithm 5 with this shared interruptible cap produces A_alpha,b+4: under the distance promise it returns an evaluated feasible genuine normal certificate of norm <=epsilon within C_p(1+Q_R^alpha)L_A(R,epsilon)^(b+4) original queries and its cap does not interrupt. Without the promise it remains finite, its cap has the same order, and it accepts only an actually verified certificate. Before balancing K, the total cost is bounded by C_p L_A(R,epsilon)^(b+4)[K+1+(Q_R/(K+1))^gamma].
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean R^d; induced multilinear derivative norm. Known nonempty compact convex X with diam(X)<=D and feasible x0. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for all u in X}. F is monotone, C^(p-1) on a neighborhood and Lip(D^(p-1)F)<=Lp. Q_R=Lp R^p/epsilon; L_A(R,epsilon)=1+log(2+D/R+Q_R); L_S(mu,delta)=1+log(2+Lp D^(p-1)/mu+Lp D^p/delta+mu D/delta). H_m=sum_{i=1}^m 1/i and H_0=0. S_gamma,b on (G,w,mu,delta) returns (y,n,G(y)), y in X, n in N_X(y), ||G(y)+n||<=delta, using at most C_S[1+(Lp r^(p-1)/mu)^gamma]L_S(mu,delta)^b queries, where r=||w-zstar_G|| is analysis-only. The additive convention applies at r=0.
statement.parameter_domains: d>=1; fixed p>=2, b>=0, 0<gamma<=1; 2/3<=a=(p-1)gamma<=2; 0<R<=D; Lp,D,epsilon>0. Constants may depend on fixed p and the fixed certified interface/exponents, not on dimension or instance parameters.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For each fixed certified interface in this scope and every compatible admissible F and public input, the construction supplies the Definition 5.1 certified residual interface. The hierarchy uses deterministic implementations; no expected-budget or probabilistic replacement of the given interface is asserted.

summary: A certified true-distance-sensitive strong interface S_gamma,b yields a finite capped residual interface A_{gamma/(1+gamma),b+4} when 0<gamma<=1 and 2/3<=(p-1)gamma<=2.
title: Theorem 8.1: extrapolated Halpern exponent transformation
use_when: Transfer an established strong-interface query bound to a supplied-distance monotone residual bound.
Use aggregate block energy; do not infer pointwise acceleration or constant per-inner-solve cost.
